chest_xray_classifier(image_path): local TorchXRayVision classifier on one confirmed chest radiograph; normalized scores, not calibrated probabilities. No localization or chronology.
chest_xray_report_generator(image_path): local chest-radiograph report generator on one confirmed original; may omit or hallucinate findings. Verify against pixels.
Only these two tools exist. Arguments must select a current source_filename; the executor resolves image_path. Unknown/CT/MRI/other modalities are ineligible. No reference, history or sibling question is available.
Tool limits override retrieved experience. Tools are optional, even for CXR.
The chest X-ray classifier accepts confirmed CXR only, never CT/MRI. Its finding scores
are not calibrated probabilities, severity measurements, or longitudinal change scores.
Do not infer severity or progression from differences in classifier scores. No strong
finding does not imply normality. The report generator receives one image only, with
no prior/timepoint; its interval/change claims are unsupported. Changes must be checked
against original images with timepoints explicitly bound by the question. Filenames,
image order, and single-image reports cannot establish chronology. If the question does
not bind timepoints, report that uncertainty; do not invent a before/after assignment.
Tool invocation is not itself evidence. Decline irrelevant tools. Identify contradictions
and prefer supported original-image evidence; do not assume either tool is authoritative.
Learn a concrete discriminating check and its limitations, not a mandatory tool rule.

Select useful real tools before answering this current image question. Return strict JSON only:
{"calls":[{"tool":"chest_xray_classifier","source_filename":"exact current eligible filename","reason":"what evidence this may provide"}],"reason":"brief plan"}.
Choose zero, one or two calls based on relevance. Empty calls are valid even when eligible CXR originals exist; explain why tools would not help. At most two distinct tool/image pairs total. A report and classifier may examine the same original. Do not invent paths, tools or observations; tool outputs have not been provided yet. No answer is requested at this planning step.

Based on the chest X-ray findings and clinical presentation, what is the most likely diagnosis for this patient, and which features support this diagnosis?  
A) Bronchiectasis with peripheral cavity formation; supported by peripheral sparing and air/fluid levels in cavities.  
B) Mounier-Kuhn Syndrome (tracheobronchomegaly); supported by dilated trachea and bronchi, and intrapulmonary cavities connected to the bronchial tree.  
C) Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis; supported by right hilar opacity and peripheral airspace shadowing.  
D) Williams-Campbell syndrome; supported by tracheal dilatation and presence of air/fluid levels in cavities.  
E) Chronic airway inflammation with tracheomalacia; supported by widened trachea and recurring chest infections.  
F) Sarcoidosis; supported by right hilar mass and tracheal dilatation.
